channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 50 studies (2,147 participants) found that manual therapy induces short-term neurophysiological modulation with technique-specific responses. Joint mobilization significantly increased skin conductance (sympathetic marker) versus sham in healthy cohorts, while non-HVLA soft tissue techniques were associated with reduced heart rate and increased RMSSD (parasympathetic marker).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Paired comparison of extrinsic feedback effects on motor learning and functional recovery after stroke: a secondary analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A secondary analysis of five RCTs (n=149) found that extrinsic feedback significantly improved motor learning (SMD 1.19; 95% CI 0.16-2.22) in stroke survivors, but effects on functional recovery were not significant (SMD 1.00; 95% CI -0.42-2.42), with no statistical difference between the two outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioural therapy reduces pain in patients with chronic patellofemoral pain: a multicentre randomised controlled trial.
item.description: An 8-week smartphone-based multidisciplinary digital therapeutic combining exercise and cognitive-behavioral therapy reduced usual knee pain by 12.5 mm (95% CI -17.1 to -7.8) on a VAS at 8 weeks, with improvements in pain, knee function, quality of life, and psychological outcomes, compared to education and exercise instruction in 216 patients with chronic patellofemoral pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Novel Telerehabilitation Interventions for Stress Urinary Incontinence : A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 13 RCTs found telerehabilitation-delivered pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) to be a safe, feasible, and effective modality for stress urinary incontinence (SUI), showing significant subjective symptom reductions and improved quality of life, with comparable efficacy to conventional care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Invisible Harms, Visible Benefits? Adverse Event Reporting in Physical Activity Interventions for Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Meta-analysis and Critical Appraisal
item.description: This meta-analysis and critical appraisal examines adverse event reporting in physical activity interventions for individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders, finding that current reporting practices are inadequate.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Tailoring Resistance Exercise for Knee Osteoarthritis: An Intervention Systematic Review With Dose-Response Meta-analysis of the Effects of Intensity and Volume.
item.description: A dose-response meta-analysis of 20 RCTs (n=791) found that isotonic resistance training may reduce pain (MD, -3.52 at 6000 repetitions), improve function (MD, -16.66 at 2600 repetitions), and increase muscle strength (standardized MD, 0.12 at 1600 repetitions) in knee OA patients, with moderate intensity yielding the greatest estimated benefits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Efficacy of Exercise Therapy for Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain According to the FITT Principle: A Systematic Review With Meta-analyses.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analyses found that exercise therapy following the FITT principle is effective in reducing disability in individuals with nonspecific chronic low back pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proximal and Distal Bimanual Motor Skill Learning After Stroke: Impairments, Trajectories, and Clinical Contributors
item.description: A randomized trial with 97 (sub)acute stroke patients found impairments in bimanual motor skill learning, particularly in distal upper limb segments, compared to healthy individuals.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of ankle-foot orthosis-related conditions on muscle activity, spasticity, and psychosocial outcomes after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies (N=931 participants) evaluated the effects of ankle-foot orthoses (AFOs) after stroke, finding uncertain effects on lower-limb muscle activity, spasticity, and psychosocial outcomes, despite their common use for gait improvement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Proprioception Training and Surrogate Outcomes: A Systematic Review of Definitions, Measures, and Effectiveness Claims
item.description: A systematic review explored the definitions, measures, and effectiveness claims of proprioception training, revealing significant heterogeneity in its conceptualization and application across rehabilitation and sports practices.
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Gait Speed Changes in Stroke Rehabilitation Motor Lower Extremity Randomized Controlled Trials by Intervention and Time Post-Stroke: A Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A meta-analysis of 106 RCTs found that motor lower extremity stroke rehabilitation interventions in the acute/subacute phases demonstrated significantly greater magnitude of improvement in gait speed compared to those in the chronic phase, with treadmill training, body weight-supported treadmill training, and exoskeletons showing significant benefits acutely.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical outcomes and satisfaction among low back pain patients following orthopedic manual therapy: systematic review
item.description: This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of orthopedic manual therapy (OMT), including spinal manipulation, mobilization, and soft tissue techniques, for low back pain (LBP), aiming to systematically evaluate its impact on clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction amidst varied existing evidence.
item.author: Bull Fac Phys Ther

item.title: Reliability, Device Agreement and Validity of Load–Velocity Profiles: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the reliability, device agreement, and validity of load–velocity (LV) profiles for one-repetition maximum (1RM) prediction. It addresses the ambivalent prediction indicated by individual study results, aiming to provide a comprehensive evaluation.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Home-based digital exercise versus hospital physiotherapy for plantar fasciitis: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study with dual-perspective cost-utility evaluation.
item.description: A propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study in China (n=587) found that a 12-week home-based digital exercise program was non-inferior to hospital physiotherapy for 3-month first-step morning pain in plantar fasciitis (adjusted mean difference -0.63 points, 95% CI -0.92 to -0.35; p < 0.001) and was less costly from both payer and societal perspectives.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing patient expectations as therapeutic targets in musculoskeletal care.
item.description: This Professional Practice article argues that patient expectations (PEs) are modifiable, therapeutic targets, extending beyond treatment to relational, contextual, lifestyle, spiritual, and cultural dimensions. Reconceptualizing PEs as dynamic and co-created, physiotherapists can deliver person-centered care by systematically assessing and aligning PEs with prognosis through shared decision-making.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Social Determinants of Health on Physical Therapy Utilization in Home Health and Outpatient Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 74,937 Medicare beneficiaries found that social determinants of health (SDOH) at patient, hospital, and regional levels influenced home health and outpatient physical therapy utilization after lower extremity joint replacement. Black patients had more visits, while dual-eligibility status was associated with more home health but fewer outpatient visits. Greater socioeconomic vulnerability was linked to more home health and outpatient visits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Developing biopsychosocial competence in musculoskeletal pain care: Australian physiotherapy educators' perspectives.
item.description: A qualitative study with 18 Australian physiotherapy educators identified five themes, or 'translation levers,' crucial for developing biopsychosocial competence and facilitating its clinical adoption in musculoskeletal pain care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Impact of Upper Extremity Rehabilitation on Fatigue in Individuals With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of nine studies (n=250) on upper extremity rehabilitation for fatigue in PwMS found insufficient evidence to draw definitive conclusions, with low to very low certainty of evidence.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Effect of Robot-Assisted Gait Training on Balance, Gait and Kinesiophobia in Individuals With Post-Stroke Hemiparesis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind, parallel-group RCT (n=60) found that adding robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) to conventional rehabilitation significantly improved balance, gait, walking speed, balance confidence, and kinesiophobia in individuals with post-stroke hemiparesis, with a between-group difference in KCS total score of -0.36 (95% CI: -0.51 to -0.21).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Manual Lymph Drainage in Lower Extremity Lymphedema Management: An Essential Component or An Optional Extra? A Single-Blind, Randomized Non-Inferiority Trial
item.description: This single-blind, randomized non-inferiority trial aims to determine if compression bandaging alone is non-inferior to compression bandaging combined with manual lymphatic drainage for reducing limb volume, tissue stiffness, and skin/subcutaneous thickness in Stage 2–3 lower extremity lymphedema.
item.author: Archives of PM&R
